attack_mechanism: Probing `aes_cipher_top.u0.u1.a` at a known expansion cycle discloses that key-schedule byte without an additional unknown transformation. This behavior is connected through `aes_cipher_top.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.w[3] -> aes_cipher_top.u0.tmp_w -> aes_cipher_top.u0.u1.a`. `aes_cipher_top.u0.u1.a` is one rotated byte selected directly from `w[3]` before substitution. With `kld = 0`, `w[3]` drives `tmp_w`; four byte S-boxes rotate/substitute its bytes to form `subword`, which is XORed into every next key word. The candidate leaks key-schedule bytes that can be combined with other word observations to recover the AES-128 master key.
